assumptions: Field labels (holder offsets, node stride, string offsets) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.
The string fields are described as pointer/capacity pairs because each frees (pointer, capacity + 1) unless the pointer equals the node base + 0x18; no wider type claim is made.
The buffer-exit comparison against holder+0x30 is recorded as observed; reading +0x30 as an inline-storage base is an inference, not a claimed layout.
behavior: List teardown with a per-node string dispose, then a buffer clear: drain the linked list at holder+0x10 (0x38-byte nodes, next at +0x00, string pointer at +0x08 with capacity at +0x18, short-form rule, node freed at size 0x38, head to tail), memset the holder+0x00 buffer with count * 8 zero bytes where count is the qword at holder+0x08, zero holder+0x10 and holder+0x18, then free the buffer at size count * 8 unless its begin equals holder+0x30, in which case return plainly. Writes nothing else, never frees the holder itself, performs no canary check.

buffer_tail.free_condition: begin equals holder+0x30 returns plainly, otherwise tail-jump sized delete

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

list.order: head to tail; next loaded before the node is disposed
